differences.judge_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that a think/don't-think stance vector from WSB's directed_modulation items lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83 on this model.
differences.what: contribution.md reports the prior work's own baseline-to-result lift (0.14 to 0.83) on this model, giving the judge a direct performance comparison to the prior method; the final message omits this figure entirely, only noting the submission's own pass@10 of 0.7843 vs its own baseline of 0.1275.

rationale: Both documents name the same prior source (Raman et al. 2026 / White-Bear Steering) and both admit the method applies the same think/don't-think stance-contrast principle but builds the direction from entirely self-authored prompts, concepts and carrier sentences rather than WBS's directed_modulation items, framing this as the basis for novelty. The judge-facing contribution.md additionally reports the prior paper's own performance numbers (0.14→0.83) on this model, which is not repeated to the user, but this is a minor omission rather than a change in how the source, overlap, or novelty are characterized.
